notes: All 28 source and 34 target IDs are partitioned exactly once.

מִלֵּא אֶת־יָדוֹ is fused onto consecrated under rule 30, the passive auxiliaries being construction-supplied; the marker and the suffix are left unrepresented, and splitting the idiom would leave יָד with no English at all.
The even before the holy garments is added: no marker and no לְ stands on that phrase, which is rule 16's stated limit — contrast vv. 16 and 21, where a לְ does stand and takes the word.
תַּחַת takes the discontinuous in … stead headed on stead (rules 25, 30), and both linen/holy garments phrases follow rule 29's fronting case as at v. 23.
